docRequirement: worktrees.md:112 (§ Choose the base branch) binds the default `worktree.baseRef: "fresh"` path to refreshing the remote ref before branching: "For a `\"fresh\"` base, Claude Code keeps `origin/HEAD` current: when the repository hasn't been fetched in the last 24 hours, it fetches the default branch, capped at five seconds, and uses the locally cached ref if the fetch fails." The same line pins the two fallbacks we already honour: "If no remote is configured, or `origin/HEAD` isn't cached locally and can't be fetched, the worktree falls back to your current local `HEAD`", and names our behaviour as the superseded one: "Before v2.1.208, a fresh worktree used whatever `origin/HEAD` was already cached locally."
current: We resolve `origin/HEAD` but never refresh it. `worktreeBaseShaCandidates` (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/worktree-git-plan.ts:39-53) returns, for `baseRef: 'fresh'`, exactly two candidates: `{ operation: 'base-fresh', cwd: 'repo', args: ['-C', repoRoot, 'rev-parse', 'origin/HEAD'], allowFailure: true }` (worktree-git-plan.ts:50) then `{ operation: 'base', args: ['-C', repoRoot, 'rev-parse', 'HEAD'] }` (worktree-git-plan.ts:43-47). There is no fetch, no last-fetch staleness check and no default-branch resolution. The sole production consumer is the lease policy at packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:10150, which loops the candidates and takes the first non-empty sha (SessionManager.ts:10149-10155); the import is SessionManager.ts:136. `WorktreeGitCommand` (worktree-git-plan.ts:16-23) has no per-command timeout field, and every worktree git child runs with one fixed `timeoutMs: 60_000` (SessionManager.ts:10043) under `profile: 'read-only'` with `additionalWritableRoots: [authority.root, authority.namespaceRoot]` (SessionManager.ts:10041, 10131). Repo-wide `grep -ran "'fetch'" --include='*.ts' packages apps` returns only WebFetch permission-DSL tests (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/permission-dsl.test.ts:129,331,334) and one schema fixture (packages/shared/src/__tests__/unified-network-interceptor.schema.test.ts:327) — zero git-fetch call sites, with `origin/HEAD` grep as the positive control on the same files. The gap is asserted by a test: packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/worktree-git-plan.test.ts:14-18 pins the exact two-candidate argv, and :26-29 pins that the resolved default's first candidate contains `origin/HEAD`. Two comments claim the parity we do not have: packages/shared/src/config/worktree-settings.ts:68-69 ("Documented default for `baseRef` is `\"fresh\"` and we match it") and packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:51-54 ("The base-branch half of that sentence is already satisfied here").
divergence: Not a wrong key or a wrong value — a missing step. Our `origin/HEAD` read is correct and both documented fallbacks are correct; what is absent is the freshness prelude the page added in v2.1.208: (a) no 24-hour last-fetch staleness gate, (b) no `git fetch` of the default branch, (c) no five-second cap for that fetch (the 60s process timeout at SessionManager.ts:10043 is the generic worktree-git budget, not the doc's cap, and is moot while no fetch is issued), (d) no `remote set-head`-style recovery for a repository where `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` was never written (a `git init` + `git remote add` + `git fetch` clone), which today drops straight to local `HEAD`. Net effect: `git rev-parse origin/HEAD` resolves a purely local remote-tracking ref that only moves on fetch, so every "fresh" worktree in a repo the user has not fetched today branches off the stale cached commit — literally the pre-v2.1.208 behaviour the page calls out as changed.

change.what: Add `timeoutMs?: number` to `WorktreeGitCommand` (documented as the per-command cap, absent means the caller's default). Widen `worktreeBaseShaCandidates(repoRoot, baseRef)` to `worktreeBaseShaCandidates(repoRoot, baseRef, freshness?: { lastFetchedAtMs?: number; nowMs: number; originHeadCached: boolean })` so the freshness decision stays a pure, table-testable argv mapping — the file's own rationale at :12-13. For `baseRef === 'head'` the result is unchanged. For `'fresh'`, when `freshness` is supplied and `lastFetchedAtMs === undefined || nowMs - lastFetchedAtMs >= 86_400_000`, prepend `{ operation: 'base-fetch', cwd: 'repo', args: ['-C', repoRoot, 'fetch', '--no-tags', '--quiet', 'origin'], allowFailure: true, timeoutMs: 5_000 }`, and when `originHeadCached === false` also `{ operation: 'base-set-head', cwd: 'repo', args: ['-C', repoRoot, 'remote', 'set-head', 'origin', '--auto'], allowFailure: true, timeoutMs: 5_000 }` (that is what creates `refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` in a repo that never had it; `fetch` alone does not). Both must be `allowFailure` so a dead remote degrades to the cached ref. Crucially the prelude commands must NOT terminate the candidate loop on success — see the SessionManager entry. Omitting `freshness` keeps today's two-candidate output, so no caller is forced to change at once. Replace the `"fresh"` paragraph of the doc comment at :26-38 with the v2.1.208 rule and cite worktrees.md:112. Not a one-liner, but small: one new optional field, one new parameter, two new command literals.

Three edits in one file. (1) `runWorktreeGit` (:10020-10048): add a trailing `timeoutMs = 60_000` parameter and pass it at :10043 instead of the literal, so the doc's five-second cap is expressible. (2) The `runGit` closure (:10117-10133): add a `timeoutMs?: number` parameter and thread it into `runWorktreeGit`. (3) `policy.select` (:10144-10161): before the candidate loop, when `worktreeSettings().baseRef === 'fresh'`, learn the two freshness inputs — the shared git dir via `runGit(root, ['-C', root, 'rev-parse', '--git-common-dir'], 'git-common-dir', true)` (needed because a session root can itself be a worktree, worktrees.md:108) then `statSync`/`stat` the `FETCH_HEAD` inside it for `lastFetchedAtMs` (missing file ⇒ never fetched ⇒ stale), and `originHeadCached` from `runGit(root, ['-C', root, 'symbolic-ref', '--quiet', 'refs/remotes/origin/HEAD'], 'origin-head-cached', true).exitCode === 0`. Pass `{ lastFetchedAtMs, nowMs: Date.now(), originHeadCached }` to `worktreeBaseShaCandidates`. The loop at :10150-10155 currently breaks on `exitCode === 0 && baseSha`; a `fetch` exits 0 and prints nothing, so with the existing `baseSha = result.output.trim()` it would not break — but make the prelude explicit rather than incidental: skip sha capture for commands whose `operation` starts with `base-fetch`/`base-set-head`, or gate on a new `WorktreeGitCommand` discriminator. Pass `candidate.timeoutMs` through `runGit`.

The two existing `fresh` assertions (:13-18 and :26-29) pin the pre-fix argv and will fail; update them to the no-`freshness` overload (unchanged output) and add the new cases: fresh + `lastFetchedAtMs` within 24h ⇒ no fetch command; fresh + `lastFetchedAtMs` older than 24h ⇒ `base-fetch` first with `timeoutMs: 5_000` and `allowFailure: true`, `origin/HEAD` rev-parse still ahead of local `HEAD`; fresh + `lastFetchedAtMs: undefined` ⇒ treated as stale; fresh + `originHeadCached: false` ⇒ `base-set-head` present; `head` ⇒ still exactly one candidate and never a fetch. Table-drive the four fresh rows.

Line 68-69 currently reads "Documented default for `baseRef` is `\"fresh\"` and we match it". Until the fix lands that is false about the freshness half; after the fix it is true but should name the v2.1.208 refresh so the next reader does not have to rediscover it. One-line comment edit.

Lines 51-54 assert "The base-branch half of that sentence is already satisfied here: `worktreeBaseShaCandidates` resolves `origin/HEAD` first" — stale against worktrees.md:112. Correct it to say the ref is refreshed under the 24h/5s rule (post-fix) rather than merely read. One-line comment edit.

blastRadius: Narrow and in-package. `worktreeBaseShaCandidates` has exactly one production caller (SessionManager.ts:10150, imported at :136) plus worktree-git-plan.test.ts, which pins the argv and must change with it. `runWorktreeGit` has exactly one caller, the `runGit` closure at SessionManager.ts:10124. Downstream, `WorktreeLeaseService.acquire` (packages/server-core/src/pi-harness/worktree-lease-service.ts:210-220) consumes `baseSha` and refuses an empty one (:211); `git.create` (SessionManager.ts:10164) feeds it to `worktree add -b`. NO wire or schema change: `PiWorktreeLeaseV1.baseSha` is persisted through `persistManagedInteractionState` → `persistSession` (SessionManager.ts:10137-10142), but only its VALUE changes, not its shape, and `assertProvenance` (worktree-lease-service.ts:339-341) compares a lease against its own recorded sha, so leases created before the fix keep validating. Both lease-service test suites stub `policy.select` wholesale (worktree-lease-service.test.ts:19,120,148,178,193; worktree-orphan-sweep.test.ts:45), so neither is affected. It DOES cross a process-lifecycle/isolation boundary, which is a risk trigger in this repo: the fix makes a worktree git child touch the network for the first time. It is spawned via `processSupervisorPort.start` with `profile: 'read-only'` and `additionalWritableRoots: [authority.root, authority.namespaceRoot]` (SessionManager.ts:10029-10045) — `.git` lives under `authority.root` so the ref update is writable, and default egress is `open` (packages/shared/src/config/sandbox-settings.ts:830-843), but under `allowManagedDomainsOnly` the fetch is denied and MUST degrade silently, which the `allowFailure: true` + timeout path gives: a timed-out foreground child resolves rather than rejects (process-supervisor.ts:331-342, 383-397) and `runWorktreeGit` only throws when `!allowFailure` (SessionManager.ts:10046). Two user-facing surfaces sit on this path: the `EnterWorktree` tool (packages/session-tools-core/src/tool-defs.ts:1015, `visibility: 'pi-only'`) and subagent `isolation: 'worktree'` (packages/shared/src/agents/definitions.ts:56).
userImpact: Observable, silent, and it produces wrong work rather than an error. On the Pi backend, a user who runs `EnterWorktree` — or dispatches a subagent with `isolation: worktree` — in a repository they last fetched days ago gets a worktree branched off that stale `origin/main`, with no warning anywhere in the UI: the lease is created normally and the session proceeds. The agent then edits, builds and commits against a base that is missing everything merged upstream since the last fetch, so its branch conflicts on rebase, its tests can fail against removed APIs, and it can re-implement work already on main. The user's own `git fetch` cadence is the only thing keeping this correct, and nothing tells them it slipped. It does NOT bite a freshly cloned or actively fetched repo, which is why it looks fine in normal use; a long-lived checkout left unfetched over a weekend is where it shows. The one arm that IS documented-correct today is the no-remote fallback to local `HEAD`.
notes: Every file cited was read in full or over the cited range: worktree-git-plan.ts (all 124 lines), worktree-git-plan.test.ts (all 88), worktree-settings.ts (all 181), SessionManager.ts:10020-10048 and :10085-10200, definitions.ts:40-70, process-supervisor.ts:114-120/215/320-398/639-646, sandbox-settings.ts:826-876, plus greps of worktree-lease-service.ts and both its test suites. Two things the page does not specify and the change list therefore CHOOSES rather than mirrors: (1) the exact fetch argv — the doc says "fetches the default branch", it does not give a command, so `fetch --no-tags --quiet origin` (a superset that updates every `refs/remotes/origin/*`) plus `remote set-head origin --auto` for the uncached-`origin/HEAD` arm is our reading; a narrower `fetch origin <branch>` would need the branch name resolved from the cached symbolic ref first, which is an extra local command for no observable gain. (2) the staleness signal — the doc says "hasn't been fetched in the last 24 hours" without naming a source; `FETCH_HEAD` mtime under `--git-common-dir` is the standard git-observable proxy and is what the change list uses. Also unverified: whether an existing session's worktree flow has a live CDP case in docs/testing/cdp-live-checklist.md that would need a new row.
